html:
On 24 June 2018 Saudi Arabia lifted its ban on women driving, the last such ban in the world.

No written law banned it, but women could not get licences, and clerics and officials defended the rule. Women had challenged it for decades. In 1990, 47 women drove in a convoy through Riyadh and lost their jobs. In 2011 Manal al-Sharif posted a video of herself driving and was jailed for days; others repeated such protests in the following years.

The change came as part of the reforms of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, which also reopened cinemas, allowed concerts and eased the guardianship rules over women. It reversed the strict turn that followed the Grand Mosque seizure of 1979.

Weeks before the ban ended, the government arrested several of the women who had campaigned against it, including Loujain al-Hathloul, who was imprisoned for nearly three years. The message was that reform would come from the top, not from protest. Compare Turkish women winning the vote in 1934.
sum: On 24 June 2018 Saudi Arabia lifted its ban on women driving, the last such ban in the world.
